pages.text:
Getting StartedBackend Runtime Setup
Backend runtime setup

Set up Cortex in a Convex host before connecting an application. The backend runs Agent, Workflow/Workpool jobs, registered tools, Gateway inference and asynchronous memory.

1. Install and register​

Install the SDK dependency in the host as described in installation, inspect the additive plan and resolve its required-dependency report before applying it. For an explicitly selected disposable development deployment:

cortex backend install ./host --plan
cortex backend install ./host
cortex backend register ./host --target ./target.json
cortex backend provision ./host --target ./target.json --principal ./principal.json


Registration and provisioning need Convex management access and a matching dev: deployment key in environment variables (defaults CONVEX_ACCESS_TOKEN and CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY). They verify the actual team/project/deployment tuple before dispatch. These helpers are development operator commands; normal app tokens never register a backend or provision grants.

target.json selects exact positive team/project IDs, deployment name and origin:

{
  "teamId": 123,
  "projectId": 456,
  "deploymentName": "your-development-deployment",
  "deploymentUrl": "https://your-development-deployment.convex.cloud",
  "disposable": true
}


Replace the example values with the selected deployment's actual metadata. A URL or credential alone does not establish a disposable target.

2. Configure identity and trusted grants​

Configure the host's accepted JWT issuer, audience/application ID and JWKS (or its supported existing Convex auth integration). Trusted operator provisioning binds the verified issuer/subject to a principal, membership and grant.

{
  "issuer": "https://identity.example.com",
  "subject": "your-user-subject",
  "actorKind": "user",
  "tenantId": "your-tenant",
  "memorySpaceId": "your-space",
  "capabilities": ["read", "write", "run", "tool", "storage:read", "storage:write"],
  "resourceAccess": "own"
}


Grant capabilities are explicit. Supported access levels are own, space and tenant; a space grant requires a space, and a tenant grant omits the space selector. Optional expiresAt is a future Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Provision administrator/service grants only through trusted administration and for the required purpose.

The JWT identifies the actor. Caller claims, tenant labels, run IDs, local snapshots and resource IDs cannot provision grants or cross a scope boundary. Auth integration covers the token callback and view clearing.

3. Install policy and publish an Agent​

An operator installs the deployment's versioned model qualifications and policies, narrows them for tenants/Agents, and publishes an executable Agent definition through the guarded agentDefinitions:publishVersion contract. The definition pins instructions, registered tools and context-handler versions/hashes, memory mode, required stages and policy versions. Revoke a version through agentDefinitions:revokeVersion when it should no longer run.

Use runtimeModelPolicy:installDeploymentPolicy with a trusted manifest; tenant policy provisioning and qualification records are internal operator contracts. Never fabricate model qualification receipts from a provider catalog entry. A model name alone does not establish interface, structured output, tool, embedding or media support.

The model-policy guide explains operation keys, limits, replay and incurred uncertainty. Text chat needs a qualified response policy and managed query/memory embedding profile. Applications read the profile from the backend.

4. Configure the application​
cortex backend configure ./app   --url https://your-development-deployment.convex.cloud   --http-url https://your-development-deployment.convex.site   --agent-id your-agent --agent-version 1 --space your-space


This appends public metadata to .env.local, preserves existing values and refuses conflicting origins. Tokens and upstream keys are supplied separately through the host/backend configuration.

Setting	Purpose
NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL	Installed runtime origin
NEXT_PUBLIC_CORTEX_HTTP_URL	Same installation's authenticated HTTP action origin
NEXT_PUBLIC_CORTEX_AGENT_ID / NEXT_PUBLIC_CORTEX_AGENT_VERSION	Published executable definition
NEXT_PUBLIC_CORTEX_MEMORY_SPACE_ID	Optional selector narrowing the actor's current grants

Deployment keys, Gateway/provider keys, callback secrets and graph passwords stay in trusted backend/operator services. The app supplies a short-lived host JWT through fetchToken.

Optional capabilities​

Configure graph workers when graph projection is required. Private assets and media use the configured HTTP origin and retained jobs. The media guide covers service access, supported inputs and saved-operation recovery.

Continue with the quickstart or runtime client reference.

Getting StartedFirst Backend Run
First backend run

Start with an installed and configured backend: accepted host JWT, current grant, published Agent version and qualified text/embedding policies. The application needs no upstream inference key.

Vercel quickstart​
cortex templates init demo --template vercel-ai-quickstart --template-version 1.4.0 --catalog-version 1.3.0 --yes --graph none
cd demo
npm run dev


Configure .env.local with the runtime origin, HTTP action origin and Agent selectors described in configuration. Open the URL printed by Next.js, enter your host JWT in Connect, and send a message. The development token form keeps the token in memory; a host application can replace it with its identity provider callback.

Watch response and memory status separately. Use Disconnect observer, Reconnect observer and Observe an existing run to recover the retained run. Disconnect keeps backend work running; Cancel run explicitly requests cancellation. Tool/input approvals continue the same backend operation.

Basic terminal and HTTP app​
cortex templates init basic-app --template basic --template-version 1.4.0 --catalog-version 1.3.0 --yes --graph none
cd basic-app
npm start
# In a separate terminal, when the HTTP interface is needed:
npm run server


Set CONVEX_URL, AGENT_ID, AGENT_VERSION and optional MEMORY_SPACE_ID, or the generated public selector equivalents. The terminal uses CORTEX_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE (a host-managed private token file, mode 0600) or process-only CORTEX_AUTH_TOKEN. HTTP requests always provide their own Authorization: Bearer <host JWT>.

Plain input prints a request ID before submit. /send <requestId> <text>, /observe, /watch, /history, /recall <requestId> <query> and /readiness expose retained execution and memory. Keep the original identity after an ambiguous timeout.

ChatSDK​
cortex templates init chat --template chat-sdk --template-version 1.4.1 --catalog-version 1.3.0 --yes --graph none
cd chat
pnpm dev


The canonical home uses AI SDK 7 remote transport and host JWTs. Its document panel submits durable title, Markdown, code, CSV sheet and suggestion jobs. Applying a suggestion selects the exact retained artifact version. Follow the generated README for the app's manager and backend configuration.

Application development scripts start the application. Backend registration/deployment and optional graph workers are separate operator tasks. See AI SDK integration for your own React host.

The templates catalog is independently versioned at 1.3.0. The current app payloads are Basic and Vercel AI quickstart 1.4.0, and Chat SDK 1.4.1. These are upcoming release selections; the registry publication step is separate. Existing immutable app payloads remain available for their pinned versions.

pages.text:
ToolsCLI Reference
Cortex CLI reference

The upcoming CLI, SDK and provider are 0.39.0. Use Node 24.15.0+ and the declared npm 12.2.0 toolchain. The CLI selects the project's installed Convex executable. Until publication, select matching local archives explicitly.

Backend runtime setup​
cortex backend install ./host --plan
cortex backend install ./host --jwt-provider ./jwt-provider.json
cortex backend register ./host --target ./target.json
cortex backend provision ./host --target ./target.json --principal ./principal.json
cortex backend configure ./app --url https://your-deployment.convex.cloud --http-url https://your-deployment.convex.site --agent-id your-agent --agent-version 1 --space your-space
cortex backend guide


Installation composes the host functions directory/schema/components/auth/HTTP routes. Ambiguous merges are refused. --sdk-path selects an installed SDK distribution. Registration/provisioning are explicit development operator tasks with exact disposable metadata and management/target-bound credentials. Configure appends public metadata only. See backend setup for JSON shapes, qualifications and Agent publication.

Application catalog​
cortex templates list --format json
cortex templates init demo --template vercel-ai-quickstart --template-version 1.4.0 --catalog-version 1.3.0 --yes --graph none
cortex templates init chat --template chat-sdk --template-version 1.4.1 --catalog-version 1.3.0 --yes --graph none
cortex templates init basic-app --template basic --template-version 1.4.0 --catalog-version 1.3.0 --yes --graph none
cortex templates update ./demo --to 1.4.0 --catalog-version 1.3.0 --dry-run


Template IDs are basic, vercel-ai-quickstart and chat-sdk. Catalog and payload versions are independent of the SDK. CLI build does not assemble payloads. Basic/Vercel use npm; Chat follows its declared pnpm manager. Graph off needs no Docker. Application dev scripts start only the app; backend registration/deployment is explicit.

For local packages use --sdk-package, --provider-package and --templates-package. Missing versions, absent ownership and conflicting edited files fail before unsafe replacement. Dry-run plans without project/dependency/service writes; no-install stages without dependency/lock regeneration.

Interrupted external update work requires the original receipt. templates update ./demo --recover restores journaled files only; it reports reconciliation required until external effects are manually reconciled and acknowledged with --recover --yes. Recovery never repeats dependencies, backend or graph work. Do not combine recovery with version/dry-run/package override flags.

SDK/backend channel​
cortex init backend --template none --local --yes --graph none
cortex install ./existing-project --no-deploy --yes --graph none --dry-run
cortex update -d development --sdk-version 0.39.0 --convex-version 1.46.0 --sync --dry-run
cortex schema status ./host
cortex schema sync ./host --dry-run


Application and SDK update ownership stay separate. --sync explicitly synchronizes owned backend sources after a dependency update; dependency changes do not imply deployment. Preserve host schema/functions/config and repair conflicts explicitly. Existing-project install supports its declared standalone manager constraints; --no-install requires --no-deploy. Cloud staging is separate from native target setup.

The recognized old Next shim lacking MutationCtx needs its app update before SDK backend synchronization. Arbitrary/edited host schemas require explicit composition rather than guessed merging. No automatic legacy runtime data/embedding migration is included.

Target selection and native lifecycle​
cortex config add-deployment development --url https://your-deployment.convex.cloud --json-only
cortex config set-path development ./host
cortex config set-key development
cortex config show --format json
cortex use development
cortex status -d development --check
cortex doctor -d development --json
cortex dev -d development


Selection is explicit -d, project use, default, then sole deployment. Stale/ambiguous aliases fail. URL/key environment values do not override aliases. Config is private/atomic and diagnostics redact secrets. Native mutations require explicit target/path/key agreement; --local and --prod assert intent rather than silently switching targets.

dev runs one foreground Convex child and Ctrl-C stops it. Run app scripts separately. Status/doctor inspect without pruning or starting services; explicit checks are bounded. There is no detached supervisor or port-kill dashboard.

Optional graph service​
cortex graph setup ./host --graph neo4j --graph-mode local --yes --dry-run
cortex graph status ./host
cortex graph stop ./host
cortex graph start ./host


Memgraph/existing services are also supported. Credentials remain private; URIs are credential-free. Local operations validate project ownership and stop preserves volumes. Existing-service setup probes without data mutation; lifecycle is refused for resources not owned by the project. Runtime connector/service-grant/worker registration is a separate graph setup step.

Explicit domain administration​

Memory/facts/conversations/users/spaces commands operate under selected transport and data scope. Scope IDs/--scope-user/--tenant do not fabricate a JWT. Complete user export and supported-layer erasure require fixed deployment administration; omitted tenant means tenantless only. Inspect partial/unknown receipts before recovery.

Native db export uses deployment ZIPs; it is separate from domain export. Lifecycle-bearing archives/targets refuse unsupported import before mutation. Raw backup/restore/clear and protected restore sessions are not an alternative. schema references and explicit supported migration are distinct from status/install/help; no automatic runtime legacy migration follows.

Use leaf --help for exact formats/options. Completion is explicit script output (completion bash|zsh|fish) and does not edit shell RC files.

The templates catalog is independently versioned at 1.3.0. The current app payloads are Basic and Vercel AI quickstart 1.4.0, and Chat SDK 1.4.1. These are upcoming release selections; the registry publication step is separate. Existing immutable app payloads remain available for their pinned versions.

What's New
What's new
Upcoming 0.39.0​

SDK, CLI and AI SDK provider 0.39.0 introduce the backend-owned Cortex runtime. This is upcoming release documentation; registry publication is separate.

Convex Agent/Workflow/Workpool execution with one canonical transcript, administrator locks and tracked edits.
Asynchronous facts/chunks/vectors, authorized pending context, contiguous watermarks and strict stage barriers.
Versioned per-operation model/interface/capability controls, shared budgets, conservative unknown costs and safe replay/fallback for primary and secondary calls.
Verified host JWT identity, trusted current grants, revocation/deletion/tombstone fencing.
Additive installation/registration/configuration, current managed embedding profiles and optional trusted graph workers.
Private Convex assets capped at 20,000,000 bytes, retained image/video jobs, signed callbacks and saved-operation reconciliation.
Browser-safe TypeScript runtime client and AI SDK 7 remote transport with approvals, reconnect and independent status.
Backend-runtime Basic, Vercel quickstart and ChatSDK applications; durable titles/documents/code/sheets/suggestions.

Application payloads and catalog have independent versions; SDK updates do not overwrite an app. See installation, backend setup and AI SDK 7.

The Python SDK is archived and this release supplies no Python runtime parity. It also includes no automatic legacy transcript/data/embedding migration, external media storage or image understanding/OCR/visual embeddings.

Historical releases​

The dated entries below preserve the released changelog. Commands, dependency versions, compatibility and status statements describe their historical releases. Use the upcoming 0.39.0 guides above for current installation/execution; historical Python entries do not imply a current runtime client.

pages.text:
ArchitectureModel Policy and Budgets
Model policy and budgets

All billable calls run through backend model-policy admission, including secondary calls. A browser submits a product intent; it cannot select an upstream model/provider, options, budget, tool result or generated context.

Versioned operations​
Operation key	Purpose
agent.respond	Agent response
memory.extract	Structured memory extraction
facts.resolve	Fact resolution/revision
memory.summarize	Source/context summaries
embedding.query / embedding.memory	Query and memory embeddings
conversation.title	Retained conversation title
artifact.text / artifact.code / artifact.sheet	Content generation
artifact.suggestions	Version-bound proposed edits
media.image.generate / media.video.generate	Retained media generation

Deployment policy establishes qualified bounds. Tenant and Agent/version policies narrow those rules. Trusted overrides are recorded with actor/change/authorization evidence; caller input cannot manufacture an override.

Policy checks include allowed models and native interfaces, capabilities, options, tool registry, input/context/output tokens, tool steps, timeout, operation/run/tenant budgets and concurrency. Prompt/schema/extraction/tool-registry/price/bound revisions are pinned. A model catalog listing does not establish compatible tools, structured output, embedding, image or video support.

One operation identity​

Semantic identity binds the request to scope, source revision, policy and model/interface version. Stable request IDs replay the same intent; changed input under the same identity conflicts. Reconnect and observation never create another paid operation.

Fallback requires its own qualified policy and admission/reservation. It remains under the original logical operation/run budget and cannot follow an unknown or already visible effect as a fresh attempt. Automatic titles share the actual parent Agent budget; explicit content jobs include their secondary title within one job budget.

Unknown costs and outcomes​

Qualified cost ceilings cover all provider charges at the admitted caps. Missing charge information is conservative incurred uncertainty, not zero. An unknown upstream outcome can retain a liability and concurrency slot until terminal evidence supports settlement.

A local timeout, cancel or deadline alone does not establish upstream terminality. It cannot refund a reservation, free an uncertain slot or authorize a blind retry. Recovery reconciles the saved operation. Unsupported capabilities and policy/budget denial are explicit results.

See resilience, artifacts and media.

Documentation Overview
Cortex documentation

Cortex runs stateful AI agents on Convex. Your application supplies verified identity, submits user input and renders retained output. The backend owns inference, tools, the executable transcript and asynchronous memory.

These docs describe the upcoming 0.39.0 SDK, CLI and AI SDK integration. Package publication is a separate release step. Before publication, use matching locally built package archives; installation examples that select a registry version apply once that version is available. Application templates use an independent version channel.

Build an application​
Install the backend into a new or existing Convex host.
Configure identity, grants and a published Agent.
Connect the TypeScript runtime client, or use AI SDK 7 with React.
Observe response, memory and graph status independently; reconnect to the retained run.
Understand the runtime​
Topic	Start here
Agent, Workflow and Gateway ownership	System overview
Canonical history and tracked edits	Conversation history
Pending context and consistency	Memory orchestration
Every model call and its budget	Model policy
Private files and durable generation	Assets and media
Verified identity and revocation	Authentication
Optional Neo4j and Memgraph projection	Graph integration

The lower-level SDK reference remains available for explicit memory APIs and server administration. Ordinary applications use the remote runtime path. The Python SDK is archived; this runtime has a TypeScript client.
